title: Assessing Social Alignment: Do Personality-Prompted Large Language Models Behave Like Humans?

live_model.evidence: Fig. 12 model list: "...gpt-3.5-turbo-0125 / gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 / gpt-4o-2024-05-13 / gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18" -- trait-alignment plot across LLMs

prompt.location: Methodology (BFI-44 personality-prompting templates; Milgram Experiment replication protocol)
prompt.note: Models are prompted to exhibit specific Big-Five trait levels, then assessed via the BFI-44 questionnaire and a Milgram-style obedience simulation.

claim.metric: alignment between prompted and BFI-44-measured personality trait value (Agreeableness/Conscientiousness/Openness)
claim.location: Figure 12 (per-model trait-alignment plot, gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 row); exact numeric alignment value not confirmed in the excerpt read

data.source: BFI-44 personality inventory (standard public instrument); Milgram Experiment paradigm (public, well-documented)

notes: gpt-4o-2024-05-13 is also directly tested in the same paper (also on the live list) and is the focus of a separate Milgram-experiment checkpoint-comparison (Figure 13, vs. gpt-4o-2024-08-06). Marked 'maybe': the specific trait-alignment number for gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09 (as opposed to a qualitative figure position) was not confirmed in the excerpt read.
